title: Nudgeflow Mini Scenario Simulator for Batch + Cache Policies
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a compact, scenario-driven simulator (Nudgeflow) embedded in the Redwood Console that helps operators compare small policy presets for batching and KV/prefix caching. The simulator focuses on micro-experiments: single-route micro-presets, risk bands, token-cost delta previews, and a lightweight rollback path. The goal is to reduce decision friction when choosing between conservative and aggressive cache/batch settings and to provide clear, in-context explainers for trade-offs.
background: PM research showed customers hesitate to change cache/batching heuristics due to unclear cost/latency trade-offs and fear of regressions. Existing prototype work covers broad policy editors and long-form wizards; this ticket is for a compact, scenario-first UI intended for fast iteration and A/B rollouts.
goals: Surface 3 micro-presets (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) with one-line trade-off summaries
Show per-request median latency, 95th latency, and token cost delta for a selected workload trace
Explain prefix cache behavior in a single-line tooltip with link to detailed doc
Provide an in-console 'quick rollback' that reverts to previous policy and annotates the metric change
Add guardrail hints (safety banding) to prevent policies that violate platform SLOs
out_of_scope: Full policy composer for multi-route global rollout (handled by rollout canvas ticket)
Long-form training/eval workflows (handled by Optimize team)
acceptance_criteria: Prototype in Figma with interactive states for select route, preset selection, and rollback flow
Microcopy reviewed and approved by PM and Research
Design tokens and color usage conform to Console theme variables
Developer handoff with annotated spec (behaviors + API contract) and a GitHub issue referencing server-side endpoints
Usability test (n=6) with product engineers shows users can pick a preset and identify likely cost impact within 2 minutes
review_feedback: 2026-03-05 - Daniel R: Loved the scenario card layout; asked for clearer lineage to rollout (add 'Apply to rollout' CTA)
2026-03-07 - Lina G: Requested explicit API contract example for backend telemetry sampling; noted that cost delta must show expected variance (± band)
2026-03-09 - Noah P: Suggested color adjustments to risk bands to meet accessibility; proposed using patterned textures in condensed list for color-blind users
2026-03-12 - Priya N: Research suggests adding a 'simulate 10 requests' mode to expose cold vs warm prefix cache behavior
decisions: Use three presets (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) rather than freeform in the mini-sim to lower cognitive load
Display median and p95 latency plus token-cost delta with an uncertainty band (+/- 1 std) as a small sparkline
Guardrails will be enforced client-side in UI with a confirmation modal if selected preset is projected to exceed customer's latency SLO or token budget
Rollback will be implemented as a single-click revert that creates a tagged policy version and triggers an audit log entry
implementation_notes: Frontend: compact card list component with inline help icons; include keyboard navigation and focus states
Backend: endpoint /simulate-policy that accepts route_id + preset_id + sample_window and returns cost/latency distribution
Telemetry: annotate simulation runs with session_id for later analysis
Security: ensure audit log includes user id and snapshot of prior policy
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: customers may misinterpret sim numbers as guarantees. Mitigation: add explicit microcopy: 'Estimates based on sampled traffic; real results may vary'
Risk: overfitting to the sampled trace. Mitigation: allow switching sample windows and an option to 'Compare against historical 7-day baseline'
Risk: accidental rollout. Mitigation: require 'Apply to rollout' to open a canary targeting modal with explicit confirmation
